intro_html: Pillowy potato gnocchi baked right in a beefy marinara with pockets of ricotta and a melted mozzarella top. Each serving delivers 37 grams of protein for about $2.82. It is lasagna comfort with a fraction of the assembly work.
cost_closing_html: About $2.82 a bowl for a baked pasta dish the casual Italian places list at $15. The gnocchi never even gets boiled separately, so you save on dishes too.
shop_smart: Shelf-stable gnocchi runs about $1.97 a pack here and cooks straight in the sauce, no boiling pot, no waste.
The 93/7 beef is $21.60, over half the batch cost. Time this recipe to the 4 lb pack sale and the per-bowl price drops fast.
Jarred marinara at four store brand jars for $7.29 beats making sauce from canned tomatoes once you count the herbs, oil, and simmer time.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 400F. In a big oven-safe pot, brown the ground beef with the diced onion, breaking it up as it cooks, until no pink remains.
Add the garlic and Italian seasoning and cook 1 minute, then season with salt and black pepper.
Pour in the marinara sauce with a splash of water, bring it to a simmer, and stir in the uncooked gnocchi. Simmer 3 to 4 minutes, stirring so nothing sticks.
Dollop the ricotta over the top and scatter on the mozzarella.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes until the cheese is melted and the sauce bubbles at the edges. Rest 5 minutes.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty pot number you wrote down, and divide by 14. Scoop that weight into each container and every serving lands at about 561 calories and 37 grams of protein.

head.description: Ground beef baked gnocchi meal prep: 561 calories and 37g protein at about $2.82 a serving. Beefy marinara, pillowy gnocchi, ricotta, mozzarella.
head.keywords: baked gnocchi, ground beef gnocchi, gnocchi meal prep, budget dinner recipe, cheap pasta bake, high protein pasta
steps: Brown the ground beef with onion, then add garlic and Italian seasoning.
Stir in marinara and the uncooked gnocchi; simmer a few minutes.
Dollop with ricotta, top with mozzarella, and bake at 400F until bubbly, 15 to 20 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes and portion into 14 containers.
